label: Stream
description: Stream a bus to the caller of this run, one chunk per message, until the bus closes: an LLM's reply as it is generated, a watched query keeping a page live. Behind a Route the response body streams; behind a Socket each message is one frame and the socket stays open. Stored files inside messages go out as `{ url, mimeType, filename, sizeBytes }`.

inputs.name: bus
inputs.description: The bus to stream, from the earliest message still buffered; its closing ends the stream.

inputs.name: first
inputs.description: One value sent ahead of the bus, framed like the messages (an id, a created row, a session token).

inputs.name: format
inputs.label: Format
inputs.description: HTTP framing (ignored on a socket). `ndjson`: one JSON value per line, payloads exact. `sse`: `data:` lines and a blank line per message; readers must strip exactly one space after the colon. `raw`: payloads as-is, no separator.

inputs.name: answerAs
inputs.label: Answer as
inputs.description: Shape of each `raw` message and of socket frames; empty follows the trigger's `dataType`.

inputs.name: status
inputs.label: Status
inputs.description: HTTP status (Route only), sent with the first chunk.

inputs.name: headers
inputs.description: Extra response headers (Route only); a content-type here overrides the format's.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: True once the bus closed and the last chunk was handed over.

then.message: Stream '{id}' answers nobody: no trigger with a live caller (a Route, a Socket) starts a run that reaches it. Wire it from the trigger's run (through data, or `_should_flow`), or put it in a group the trigger's `_should_flow` runs.
Stream '{id}' runs after {with}, which already sent the response's head to the HTTP caller, so this stream can never go out. Send everything through one Stream, and end the exchange with a Close.
